description_full: FinVolution Group, an investment holding company, operates in the online consumer finance industry in the People's Republic of China, Indonesia, Philippines, and internationally. It operates an online consumer finance platform through its ppdai.com and PPDai mobile application; AdaKami, an online loan platform; and JuanHand for lending and other personalized financial services. The company was formerly known as PPDAI Group Inc. and changed its name to FinVolution Group in November 2019. FinVolution Group was founded in 2007 and is headquartered in Shanghai, the People's Republic of China.

financial_summary: FinVolution Group is a small-cap financial services business with a $694M market cap on $2M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -86% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +5705.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 44% against a 9% cost of capital — a 35-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $268M in free cash flow — roughly 13143 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.73× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 27.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and stock-based comp at 1098% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 26% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 881.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
